info.title: WideCast.ai Public API
info.summary: Turn plain-text scripts into AI-generated short-form videos.
info.description:
WideCast.ai turns plain-text scripts (and soon ideas, audio, existing videos)
into AI-generated short-form videos: scenes + voice + B-roll, ready for
review in the scene editor.

**Authentication**: every request needs an API key, passed as
`Authorization: Bearer wc_live_*`. Generate keys in the dashboard
(Setup Center → API Keys). Each call to `/v1/create_video` consumes
credits from your account; usage (calls + credits) is tracked per key.

## Two input flows (`source`) × two completion gates (`output_type`)

### `source` — what kind of input you provide

1. **`source: "text"`** (default) — you provide `script_text` (80-500
   words), used VERBATIM by the narrator. No AI rewriting.
2. **`source: "idea"`** — you provide `idea_text` (5-1000 words, longer
   gets auto-truncated). The server writes a narration from the idea
   (AI), then continues the same scene-sourcing flow as `text`. You
   also pick `language`, `video_length` (short/normal), and
   `research_enabled`.
3. **`source: "blog"`** — you provide `blog_text` (30-3000 words — an
   article to repurpose; longer auto-truncated). Identical pipeline to
   `idea` (same AI script-writer), just a longer input. Same optional
   `language` / `video_length` / `research_enabled`.

`idea` and `blog` are **generative sources**: the server writes the script
first (Phase 1), so they support `output_type: "text"` to stop at the
editable script. Future generative sources (audio, video) follow the
same shape.

### `output_type` — how far down the pipeline to run (pipeline depth)

1. **`output_type: "text"`** — stop after the source→script-text phase.
   Returns a `review_url` (the UI auto-detects the data is narration-only
   and opens the Script Editor). **Only valid for generative sources**
   (`source != "text"`) — for `source: "text"` you already supplied the
   script, so `text` output would echo your input (HTTP 400).
2. **`output_type: "scene"`** (default) — stop at "scenes ready for
   review". You get back a `review_url` to inspect / edit before deciding
   to render the final MP4. Optional follow-up: `POST /v1/export_video`.
3. **`output_type: "video"`** — run end-to-end without manual review.
   `result.video_url` populated when the final MP4 is ready. Use this
   when you trust the generated scenes (programmatic / batch use).

The two axes combine — every valid `source` × `output_type` pair works,
except `source: "text"` + `output_type: "text"` (rejected — see above).

## Endpoints

- **POST `/v1/create_video`** — submit `script_text`/`idea_text` + optional
  `output_type`. Returns a `widecast*` id and initial `status: "processing"`.
- **POST `/v1/export_video`** — for `output_type: "scene"` videos that
  reached `scenes_ready_for_review`, kick the final-MP4 renderer.
  Idempotent — calling twice is a no-op.
- **GET `/v1/status/{id}`** — poll until `status` is `completed` (or
  `failed`). `result.review_url` is present from the first response
  (`pending`/`processing` too) — it's a stable id-keyed page, so you can
  show it to the user immediately. The completion gate depends on the
  video's `output_type`:
    * text  → `stage: "script_ready_for_review"`.
    * scene → `stage: "scenes_ready_for_review"`.
    * video → `stage: "video_rendered"`, `result.video_url` also set.

Polling cadence: start at 5s, exponential backoff (×1.5) up to 60s. The
SDKs implement this automatically via `video.wait()`.

## Script bounds (LOCKED)

`script_text` is used **verbatim** by the narrator — no rewriting. The
bounds reflect what fits inside a short-form video:

- **Minimum 80 words** (~20s of narration) — anything shorter renders
  a useless clip.
- **Maximum 500 words** (~120s / 2 min of narration) — beyond this,
  render cost and pacing both suffer.

## Inline media in `script_text`

Drop a **direct image or video URL** into the script next to the line it
should illustrate — WideCast strips it from the narration and uses it as
that scene's visual instead of auto-sourced B-roll. Two equivalent forms:

* **Markdown image syntax** (recommended for AI-chat callers):
  `![brief scene description](https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg)`. Chat
  hosts (Claude / ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini) render the picture inline so
  the user can SEE whether the visual fits the narration before
  approving the script. The alt text doubles as the strongest possible
  scene anchor.
* **Raw URL** on its own line (works the same; backward-compatible):
  `Our cold brew steeps for 16 hours. https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg
  That mellow finish is what people come back for.`

Direct file links only (image `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.bmp/.avif/.svg`,
video `.mp4/.webm/.mov/.m4v/.avi`); page links like a YouTube watch URL
are not inlined (use `source="video_url"` for those). See the
`script_text` field for details.

## Field-requirement convention (LOCKED)

Every constraint on every field — validation bounds, enum values,
required-vs-optional, defaults — appears in **four places**, kept in
sync:

1. **OpenAPI spec** — `description`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `enum`,
   `default`. Single source devs read first.
2. **SDK constants + types** — named exports in `widecast` (Python) and
   `@widecast/sdk` (TypeScript), so callers can refer to them
   programmatically without re-typing the literal.
3. **Markdown docs** — `Field reference` table in each endpoint page.
4. **Server enforcement** — rejected requests must surface a LOCKED
   `error.code` (e.g. `script_too_short`, `invalid_output_type`).

The SDK parity test (`test_script_bounds_constants_locked` and
equivalents) imports each SDK constant and asserts the exact numeric
value — changing one surface without the others breaks the test. New
endpoints MUST follow this same pattern.

## Conventions (locked — changing = breaking)

- Snake_case JSON fields
- **ID format**: `widecast<alphanumeric>` (~20 chars). The server's new-script
  detection checks for the literal `"widecast"` substring, so SDKs/clients MUST
  not strip it. Public id == internal `topic_id` (1:1, no mapping).
- API key prefixes: `wc_live_*`
- Object marker: every resource has `"object": "<type>"`
- Status enum: `pending | processing | completed | failed`
  (`pending` ONLY covers the brief race window between create + worker
  writing the topic row; once the row exists, status is `processing` —
  the abroll worker doesn't increment `step` until the end)
- Error envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "param?",
  "doc_url", "request_id" } }`
- Error codes (v0.1.0): `account_expired | credit_exhausted |
  render_failed | unknown_error | scenes_not_ready | export_failed |
  script_too_short | script_too_long | invalid_output_type |
  invalid_source | idea_too_short | missing_idea_text |
  blog_too_short | missing_blog_text |
  missing_video_url | missing_audio_url | missing_media_file |
  unsupported_media_url | media_too_long | file_too_large |
  missing_api_key | invalid_api_key |
  invalid_language | invalid_video_length | invalid_research_enabled |
  invalid_faceless | invalid_content_type | invalid_intervention_level |
  ideas_failed | invalid_publish_input | invalid_platforms |
  no_platforms_connected | publish_not_ready | download_failed |
  publish_failed | free_tier_limit_exceeded | telegram_not_connected |
  telegram_send_failed | invalid_parse_mode | conflicting_media |
  invalid_photo_url | invalid_video_url | message_too_long |
  rate_limited | scenes_not_ready | invalid_script | invalid_by |
  invalid_field_entry | scene_not_found | unsupported_field |
  object_level_edit_disabled | remotion_spec_disabled |
  remotion_spec_not_found | remotion_spec_parse_failed |
  remotion_spec_invalid | missing_remotion_object_rect |
  invalid_remotion_add_element | invalid_remotion_add_element_kind |
  invalid_disable_overlay_value | invalid_module_id | module_not_found |
  skill_unavailable |
  missing_uploaded_overlay_url | invalid_uploaded_overlay_url |
  svg2spec_failed |
  missing_voice_file | mixed_remotion_fields | ambiguous_text |
  invalid_media_url | modify_failed | persist_failed |
  voice_upload_queue_failed | narrator_video_upload_queue_failed |
  script_not_ready | script_parse_failed | scene_geometry_failed |
  unsupported_action |
  publisher_missing | mqtt_publish_failed | no_live_editor |
  no_active_editor | browser_error |
  screenshot_publish_failed | server_fallback_failed`
- Headers (every response): `X-Request-Id`, `X-RateLimit-*`,
  `X-WideCast-Version`
- Timestamps: ISO 8601 UTC strings (e.g. `2026-05-19T17:30:00Z`)
- Pagination (future): cursor-based — see `ListEnvelope` schema

post.description:
Create a video from either a plain-text script (`source: "text"`) or
a short idea description (`source: "idea"`). The server wraps the
same background workers that power the Script Editor + Idea-to-Video
flows in the WideCast UI.

- Returns immediately with `status: "processing"` (HTTP 202). Poll
  `GET /v1/status/{id}` until terminal.
- If `wait_for_render: true`, blocks up to **60 seconds**. If render
  completes within the window, returns `status: "completed"` (HTTP 200).
  Otherwise returns the in-flight state and the client polls.

### source

- `"text"` (default — backward-compat): provide `script_text`
  (80-500 words, used VERBATIM by the narrator). Worker:
  `request_video_script_from_script`.
- `"idea"`: provide `idea_text` (5-1000 words; >1000 auto-truncated)
  plus optional `language` / `video_length` / `research_enabled`.
  Worker chain: `ai_enhance_script` (idea → narration) →
  `request_video_script_from_script` (narration → scenes).

### output_type

- `"scene"` (default): pipeline stops at scenes-ready-for-review.
  `result.review_url` is in the create response itself (safe to share
  immediately — the page handles early arrival). You can then call
  `POST /v1/export_video` to render the final MP4.
- `"video"`: pipeline auto-chains into the renderer once scenes are
  ready. `result.review_url` ships from the create response; the
  `result.video_url` field appears on completion. No manual
  `/v1/export_video` call needed.

### Agent guidance — open `review_url` inline if you can

When you surface `result.review_url` to the user, **also open it in
your built-in web viewer if your runtime exposes one** (Codex
view-url, ChatGPT browse tool, any host that can iframe an external
URL, future inline browsers). The review page is a full scene
editor — letting the user inspect / swap / approve scenes inside
the same chat is dramatically better UX than asking them to
copy-paste a link into another tab. If you have no such tool, just
show the URL as a clickable link.

### Bounds (LOCKED — see SDK constants)

| Field | When required | Min words | Max words | Over-max behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `script_text` | source=text | 80 (`SCRIPT_MIN_WORDS`) | 500 (`SCRIPT_MAX_WORDS`) | reject `script_too_long` |
| `idea_text` | source=idea | 5 (`IDEA_MIN_WORDS`) | 1000 (`IDEA_MAX_WORDS`) | auto-truncate, surfaced in `details.input_truncated_from` |
| `blog_text` | source=blog | 30 (`BLOG_MIN_WORDS`) | 3000 (`BLOG_MAX_WORDS`) | auto-truncate, surfaced in `details.input_truncated_from` |

SDKs export these as named constants — refer to those instead of
hard-coding the numbers. Word count = whitespace split, works for
English + Vietnamese.

post.summary: Kick the final-MP4 renderer for an already-created video.
post.description:
Pairs with `output_type: "scene"` on `/v1/create_video`. After the
scenes-ready callback (or manual review via `review_url`), call this
to enqueue the final render.

Idempotent — calling twice is a no-op. Returns the current
`/v1/status` snapshot.

Preconditions:
- The video must have reached `scenes_ready_for_review` (HTTP 409 with
  `error.code = "scenes_not_ready"` otherwise).

Post-effects:
- The video's effective `output_type` is promoted to `"video"`.
- The completion gate becomes `result.video_url` non-empty.
- The `video.completed` webhook (if `callback_url` is set) re-arms
  and fires when the MP4 is rendered.

post.summary: Edit ONE scene (media / overlay / layout / audio / text / metadata). Free.
post.description:
Synchronous for most branches (some upload branches are async — see
below), **no credit charged** until `/v1/export_video` re-renders
the final MP4. Successful edits publish MQTT realtime to every open
scene editor so the user sees the change live.

**Agent rule — data-first**. Call `/v1/video_data` first and use
`voice_file` (the stable per-scene UID, also the base of
`{voice_file}_spec.json`) for `by`/`value`. For **layout edits**,
also call `/v1/scene_geometry` to read narrator/caption/Remotion
object boxes in 280×498 editor-preview coords without ever
rendering a screenshot. `segment.id` is only display/order metadata
and may change after reorder/add/delete.

Resolves the target scene with `by` + `value`:
  - `by="voice_file"` — exact match on the stable per-scene UID
    (preferred).
  - `by="id"` — exact match on the current `segment.id` order/display.
  - `by="text"` — fuzzy match against `segment.text`. Multi-match →
    HTTP 200 `ClarificationResponse` — ask the user to pick a
    `voice_file`, then re-call.

**Pick exactly ONE field family per call.** The only intentional
multi-family call is `layout.batch`, which composes layout-only
children (`overlay.narrator.*`, `overlay.caption.y`,
`remotion.object.rect`, `remotion.group.rect`).

**(A) Background media swap (`mediaUrl` / `mediaType`).** Roll-
aware: B-roll scene → asset IS the background (`mediaUrl`,
`brollUrl`, `thumbnailUrl`, `brollThumbnailUrl` synced); A-roll
scene → narrator and grid untouched, asset registered as
`user_asset_url` / `brollUrl`.

**(B) Upload Overlay (`remotion.upload_overlay`).** Free, agent-
supplied asset → Remotion spec (not Regenerate Overlay, which is
paid). **Two upload formats, chosen by URL extension**:

  - **📐 SVG path (PREFERRED for agent-authored overlays)** —
    URL ends `.svg` (case-insensitive). WideCast routes through
    `svg2spec`: parses the SVG, finds every
    `<g data-wc-object="name">` group, rasterizes EACH group
    ALONE on a transparent 720×1280 canvas, crops to the alpha
    bbox, and emits one Storyboard object per group with
    **pixel-perfect placement (NO auto-fit; max diff 2/255 vs
    original)**. **Required**: viewBox `0 0 720 1280` (portrait).
    Per-group attributes:

      * `data-wc-object="name"` — REQUIRED stable id/name;
        groups without it are rasterized as background.
      * `data-wc-kind` ∈ {`object`, `text`, `bar`, `mark`,
        `callout`} — inferred if missing.
      * `data-wc-anim` ∈ {`slide-up`, `slide-down`,
        `slide-left`, `slide-right`, `pop`, `grow-x`, `grow-y`,
        `fade`, …} — default `fade`; bar shapes get
        `growRight`/`growUp` automatically.
      * `data-wc-z` — paint/stack order; default = document
        order.

    Use the SVG path when you want **deterministic
    decomposition** (no classifier in the loop) plus explicit
    animation hints in one authored file. SVG-specific errors:
    HTTP 422 `svg2spec_failed` (parse / viewBox / structure
    errors with detail message), HTTP 502 (SVG download failed).

  - **🖼 Raster path (default)** — URL extension is PNG / JPG /
    WebP / GIF / etc. Pipeline classifies the uploaded image as
    `graphic` vs `realistic`, decomposes graphic images into
    objects, and falls back to a full-frame single-image overlay
    for realistic ones (strict no-AI fallback — no Nano Banana,
    no image generation). For best object-decomposed raster
    specs: portrait 9:16 transparent PNG (720×1280 preferred) or
    flat-bg graphic with large separated foreground objects/text,
    strong contrast, readable typography; avoid photo-realistic
    backgrounds, heavy gradients, vignettes, tiny dense text.

Whichever format you use, ground the asset in scene context
(`text`, `talking_point`, `visual`, `quote`, `keyword`, `type`).
Explicit opt-in to recreate an overlay even when
`remotion_spec="none"`. Response includes a cache-busted
`remotion_spec_url` and `remotion_poster_url` (server-side
inspector fallback poster).

**(C) Remotion Storyboard object-layer rect
(`remotion.object.rect`) — PREFERRED overlay layout API.** First
call `/v1/scene_geometry` and read
`boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects`; each item has `layout_id`
(e.g. `main.one_by_one`, `main.obj_03_text`), `rect` (280×498
preview), `rect_canvas` (720×1280), temporal policy, and the
update field name. Then send
`{field_name: "remotion.object.rect", value: {layout_id, x?, y?,
w?, h?, coordinate_space: "preview"|"canvas"}}` (one or more
entries). The agent edits simple visible object boxes; WideCast
maps the rect back to raw Storyboard object offsets/sizes and
keeps the group wrapper unchanged. For `one_by_one`, scene_geometry
exposes ONE logical `*.one_by_one` rect — editing it transforms
all timed sequence items together. Object-layer x/y may produce
negative raw offsets relative to the group; allowed and matches
Remotion rendering. Spec-changing edits refresh
`{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` used by server-side scene
inspector fallback.

**(D) Remotion Storyboard group rect (`remotion.group.rect`) —
low-level wrapper edit; prefer (C) for visible overlay layout.**
`value = {element_id?, x?, y?, w?, h?, coordinate_space:
"canvas"|"preview", resize_mode?:
"scale_children"|"wrapper_only"}`. Move-only (x/y) updates the
group wrapper; child objects untouched. Group x/y are NOT clamped
— `y:-120` legitimately translates a full-canvas group upward.
Resize (w/h) defaults to `scale_children` (wrapper + every child +
root `background.bbox` scale together). `wrapper_only` is advanced.

**(E) Narrator layout rect (`overlay.narrator.rect`).** Legacy
**280×498 editor preview** coords. Either send
`{x, y, w, h, visible?, animation?, borderRadius?}` or field-by-
field via `overlay.narrator.x | y | w | h`. Preserves existing
narrator metadata and source-space `segment.narrator_face` (do
NOT mutate `narrator_face` for layout edits — `scene_geometry`
converts it through the current narrator rect for display).
Marks `overlay.narrator.touched=true` so auto-fit doesn't
overwrite. No media / audio / timeline / Remotion spec changes.

**(F) Caption Y layout (`overlay.caption.y`).** 280×498 preview
coords. Updates ONLY `overlay.caption.y` plus `touched=true`. Does
NOT edit x/w/h, visibility, config/style, `segment.text`,
`segment.words`, audio, duration, or Remotion specs.

**(G) Layout batch (`layout.batch`) — one persist, one MQTT.**
Either send multiple layout fields directly OR wrap as
`{field_name: "layout.batch", value: {fields: [...]}}`. WideCast
persists `generated_video_script` ONCE and broadcasts ONE
`scene_modified` MQTT event after all children succeed. Allowed
children: `overlay.narrator.*`, `overlay.caption.y`,
`remotion.object.rect`, `remotion.group.rect`. DISALLOWED:
`mediaUrl`/`mediaType`, `voice.upload`, `narrator.upload_video`,
`remotion.upload_overlay`, `roll.active`/`roll.switch`,
`segment.text`, metadata fields.

**(H) Upload Voice (`voice.upload`) — async.** User-supplied
audio (not Use-AI-Voice). Returns
`{object: "scene_voice_upload_queued", queue_id:
"gs_{topic_id}_{voice_file}", status: "queued"}`. On completion
the server applies `words` / `text` / `duration` / following-
scene shifts / caption timelines / `narrator_face` / `recorded`
flags to `generated_video_script` and emits MQTT
`event="scene_voice_upload_applied"`. Verify with
`/v1/video_data` after.

**(I) Upload Narrator Video (`narrator.upload_video`) — async.**
User-supplied A-roll video. If target is B-roll, the server
preserves the previous background in
`brollUrl`/`brollThumbnailUrl` and applies the same roll-switch
helper as `roll.active="A"` on completion. Returns
`{object: "scene_narrator_upload_queued", queue_id, status:
"queued"}`; completion emits MQTT
`event="scene_narrator_upload_applied"`.

**(J) A/B-roll switch (`roll.active` / `roll.switch`) — sync data
switch.** Preserves both lanes (`arollUrl`/`brollUrl`) and swaps
active runtime fields (`mediaUrl`, `thumbnailUrl`, `mediaType`,
`active_roll`, `show_narrator`, audio flags, `recorded`,
`videoTrim`). On A→B mirrors the UI's `_switched` file-family
protection when files exist. No upload / transcode / generate.

**(K) Segment text correction (`segment.text`) — sync.** Updates
`segment.text`, rebuilds `segment.words` over existing audio
timings, syncs the current caption-language entry. Does NOT
change audio, duration, or following-scene timelines.

**(L) Scene metadata** — pick from this family only: `pattern`,
`visual`, `keyword`, `quote`, `talking_point`, `type`, `sub_mode`
(or `segment.<name>` / `scene.<name>` forms). `pattern` is
validated against ai_segment_text canonical values; `type` ∈
{HOOK, STAT, KEY POINT, DATA, FACT, CALL TO ACTION};
`pattern="illustration"` requires `sub_mode` ∈
{photo_with_people, photo_no_people, document, digital_ui}.
`pattern="narration_only"` auto-clears quote+visual;
`pattern="typography_only"` auto-clears visual.

**(M) Remotion add element (`remotion.add_element`) — FREE,
SYNC, ADD-ONLY**. Append a new Storyboard group/object to the
existing spec. `value = {kind, value?, label?, url?, position?,
rect?, style_token?, emphasis?}` — OR a bare string for
`kind="text"`. `kind` ∈ {`text`, `stat`, `label`, `callout`,
`image`} (aliases: `metric`/`number`→`stat`,
`badge`/`caption`→`label`; defaults to `image` when `url` /
`image` / `src` set, else `text`). Optional placement hint
`position` ∈ {top, bottom, left, right, center} for the
server-picked default rect; OR pin a rect explicitly via
`rect: {x, y, w, h, coordinate_space: "preview"|"canvas"}`
(default 280×498 preview). Optional `entry` (default `fade`),
`delay_sec`, `z_index`, `element_z_index` (default 900). The
branch **does NOT auto-fit, replace, move, or modify existing
objects** and **must be sent alone** (returns 400
`mixed_remotion_fields` if combined with other Remotion fields,
and is not allowed inside `layout.batch` directly). Requires an
enabled spec — returns 409 `remotion_spec_disabled` for scenes
where `segment.remotion_spec="none"`. Response `applied`
carries the new `element_id`, `object_id`, and
`layout_id` (= `{element_id}.{object_id}`, e.g.
`agent_add_01.add_text_1782700000000`) plus `rect` (preview),
`rect_canvas` (720×1280), `auto_fit: false`,
`cost: "free_spec_append"`, plus a `follow_up` hint. **Standard
workflow**: immediately after `remotion.add_element` returns the
new `layout_id`, call `/v1/scene_geometry` to read the
displayed rect + violations, then send a `layout.batch` carrying
a `remotion.object.rect` with that `layout_id` to land the
element inside safe zones — the initial placement is a default,
not a polished layout.

**(N) Disable overlay (`disable_overlay`) — FREE, SYNC, data
edit.** `field_name = "disable_overlay"` (aliases:
`remotion.disable_overlay`, `overlay.disable`,
`remotion_spec.none`). `value` may be `true`, the string
`"none"`, or `{enabled:false}`. **What it does**: sets
`segment.remotion_spec="none"` (the opt-out sentinel) and emits
MQTT `scene_modified` with `overlay_disabled: true`. **What it
does NOT do**: it does NOT delete `{voice_file}_spec.json`, does
NOT delete `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`, does NOT
regenerate a replacement, and does NOT touch narrator / caption
/ media / timing / layout. Must be sent **alone** — combining
with other Remotion fields returns 400 `mixed_remotion_fields`.
Re-disabling a scene that is already `remotion_spec="none"`
returns `applied.idempotent: true`. **Re-enable** by calling
(B) Upload Overlay (`remotion.upload_overlay`) or the manual
regenerate-overlay flow — those write a fresh
`{voice_file}_spec.json` and stamp the segment's `remotion_spec`
to `{voice_file}_spec.json?v={mtime}`. Errors: 400
`invalid_disable_overlay_value` / `mixed_remotion_fields`,
409 `missing_voice_file`.

**`remotion_spec="none"`**: user intentionally disabled the
overlay on that scene (via (N) Disable overlay or UI). Layout
edits return `remotion_spec_disabled`. Do NOT auto-enable —
only re-enable via (B) Upload Overlay if the user asks.

Successful edits publish MQTT realtime so open editors hot-update.
Final render cost lands when `/v1/export_video` is called again.

post.summary: Data-only scene layout geometry (cheap, no screenshot). Free.
post.description:
SYNCHRONOUS, free, read-only. **Use this after `/v1/video_data` and
before any screenshot/vision step** when an agent needs to audit
layout cheaply or pick coordinates for `/v1/modify_scene`. Resolves
the scene by stable `voice_file` (preferred), loads
`{voice_file}_spec.json` if available, and maps legacy narrator /
caption boxes plus Remotion Storyboard display boxes into one
**280×498 editor-preview** coordinate space.

Returns:
  - `coordinate_space` — `{width: 280, height: 498, unit:
    "editor_preview_px"}`.
  - `safe_zones` — `dead_top` (top 10% reserved), `dead_bottom`
    (bottom 25% reserved), `safe_rect` between them.
  - `scene` — `{text, talking_point, type, pattern, keyword,
    visual, quote, show_narrator, active_roll}`.
  - `boxes.narrator` — `{rect, visible, face_source, face,
    face_center, face_coordinate_space_note}`. `face` is the
    **displayed** face box, computed by converting source-space
    `segment.narrator_face` through the current
    `overlay.narrator.rect`. Do NOT mutate `segment.narrator_face`
    for layout edits — `narrator_face` is the source-space box for
    the narrator media and only refreshes when narrator media is
    generated/recorded/uploaded.
  - `boxes.caption` — `{container_rect, text_rect_estimate,
    visible}`. The caption box is read-only for layout decisions;
    the only mutable caption field is `overlay.caption.y` via
    `/v1/modify_scene`.
  - `boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects[]` — **the agent-facing
    layer**. Each item carries `layout_id` (e.g. `main.one_by_one`,
    `main.obj_03_text`), `rect` (280×498 preview), `rect_canvas`
    (720×1280), `temporal_policy`, and the update field name to
    pass back to `/v1/modify_scene`
    (`{field_name:"remotion.object.rect", value:{layout_id, x, y,
    w, h, coordinate_space:"preview"}}`). For `one_by_one`,
    scene_geometry exposes ONE logical `*.one_by_one` rect — the
    server transforms all timed sequence items together.
  - `boxes.remotion.groups[]` / `boxes.remotion.objects[]` /
    `boxes.remotion.sequence_objects[]` — lower-level debug data
    (STATIC/POSTER display boxes resolved with the same Storyboard
    math used by `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`).
  - `remotion_spec` — metadata for the loaded `{voice_file}_spec.json`
    (file, url, version, state). Internal `remotion_poster_*`
    keys are diagnostic-only — pass `include_diagnostics:true`
    to surface them.
  - `summary` — `{remotion_object_count,
    remotion_object_layer_count, remotion_sequence_object_count,
    remotion_group_count, remotion_temporal_policies,
    remotion_geometry_basis}`.

**Mechanical linter output is debug-only.** By default the
response is actionable data only — `violations[]` (collision
codes), `warnings[]` (mobile-readability / face-staleness hints),
and `summary.error_count` / `summary.warning_count` are
stripped. Vision-capable agents should judge collisions and
aesthetics from a screenshot via `/v1/scene_inspector`; LLM-only
agents should still proceed with the rects + `boxes.narrator.face`
to keep overlays off the face. Pass `include_diagnostics: true`
to opt back in for server/debug audits.

Designed for LLM-only agents that cannot see images: reason over
JSON, then call `/v1/modify_scene` with a `layout.batch` containing
`overlay.narrator.rect`, `overlay.caption.y`,
`remotion.object.rect` — or single-field calls. Never broadcasts
MQTT, never renders screenshots, never exposes base64 assets, and
never modifies the video.

post.summary: Upload an audio / video / image / document (or mint a pre-signed S3 PUT URL).
post.description:
Get an asset into WideCast's `widecast-assets` S3 bucket and back
out as a **public URL** the AI agent can feed into `/v1/create_video`
(as `audio_url` or `video_url`), paste into `script_text` as an
inline `![alt](url)` for images, OR `curl <get_url>` to fetch a
document body before passing it as `blog_text` / `script_text`.
This is the **canonical upload path** for AI agents handling
user-attached files — it removes the need to shop for third-party
hosts (transfer.sh / catbox / S3 of your own) or inline-base64
binary content into create_video.

**Lifecycle: the bucket prefix `assets/` auto-deletes after 24
hours.** Call `/v1/create_video` with the returned URL within that
window. Free (no credits).

**Allowed kinds**:
  * Media: `audio/*` / `video/*` / `image/*`
  * Document: `text/html` / `application/pdf` / `text/markdown`
    (HTML / PDF / Markdown — for blog drafts, research notes,
    articles the user attached to feed `source=blog`)
Anything else returns `400 unsupported_asset_type`.

**Three request shapes**:
  * `multipart/form-data` with `file=@/path/to/asset` — the standard
    multipart form upload. Best for SDKs / curl / Postman / ChatGPT
    Custom GPT Action. Server cap 500 MB. Returns
    `AssetResponse { object:"asset", url, ... }` — bytes are already
    on S3 and the URL resolves immediately.
  * `application/json` with `{ mode: "presign", filename,
    content_type }` — **the path the MCP tool dispatches through**
    (the MCP transport can't carry binary). Server mints a
    1-hour-lived pre-signed S3 PUT URL; the caller then `PUT`s the
    bytes straight to S3. Returns
    `AssetPresignResponse { object:"asset_presign", put_url, get_url, ... }`.
    The `get_url` resolves for 24 hours after the PUT lands. The
    signature binds **only the host** — the caller does NOT need to
    echo back any Content-Type / metadata header. `headers_required`
    is empty by design so `curl -X PUT --upload-file <file>
    "<put_url>"` works as-is across HTTP clients.
  * `application/json` with `{ file_data: <base64>, filename,
    content_type }` — legacy / small-file convenience for callers
    that already have the bytes inline and don't want a second
    request. Server cap 500 MB decoded; in practice the MCP
    transport caps tool args to ~25 MB, so MCP agents use the
    `mode:"presign"` shape instead.

file.description: The audio / video / image / document (HTML / PDF / Markdown) file to upload.

200.description:
Upload succeeded (multipart / base64 → `AssetResponse`) OR
pre-signed URL minted (presign → `AssetPresignResponse`).

Synchronous, free. Self-notify only — the recipient is the user who
owns this API key (delivery target is resolved server-side from

message anyone else.

**Delivery channel is auto-chosen**:
  * `telegram` — preferred when the user has completed `Connect
    Telegram` at https://widecast.ai/#setup. The message lands in
    their Telegram chat with the WideCast bot.
  * `email` — fallback when Telegram is not connected. The same
    message is delivered to the account's email address with an
    in-mail banner explaining WHY (Telegram not connected) and a
    CTA to connect. Response carries `delivery: "email"`,
    `fallback_reason: "telegram_not_connected"`, and `setup_url`.

Only returns 400 `telegram_not_connected` if the account has
NEITHER Telegram NOR an email on file. Rate-limited to 60
messages/hour/account.

Payload modes:
  * **text** — `message` only.
  * **photo** — `message` is the caption, `photo_url` is a public
    http(s) URL Telegram downloads.
  * **video** — `message` is the caption, `video_url` is a public
    http(s) URL Telegram downloads.

`photo_url` and `video_url` are mutually exclusive (Telegram can't
attach both to one message). `parse_mode` is opt-in (`Markdown` /
`MarkdownV2` / `HTML`); omit for plain text.

post.summary: Read structured scene data (data-first audit/edit entry point).
post.description:
Synchronous, free. **First step for data-first scene audit/edit** —
call this before `/v1/modify_scene` or `/v1/scene_inspector`. Returns
full annotated segment dicts in `segments`.

To keep MCP payloads usable the API trims per-segment `words` timing
arrays, top-level `captions`, and internal preview-cache fields
(`savedVideos`, `savedImages`, `_previewInstanceId`,
`_remotionSpecFetching`, `_forceNarratorRefit`). UI routes still get
full data; this is the agent-safe slim view.

**Scene identity rule** (also returned as `scene_identity` in the
response): use `voice_file` as the stable per-scene UID.
`segment.id` is only display/order metadata and may change after
reorder/add/delete. The Remotion spec for a scene is
`{voice_file}_spec.json`.

**Per-segment fields agents care about**:
  * `voice_file` (stable scene UID; use for modify/inspect).
  * `id` / `order_id` / `scene_index` (current order; UNSTABLE).
  * `type` (`A-roll` | `B-roll` | `thumbnail`).
  * `text` (narration), `talking_point`, `visual`, `quote`,
    `keyword`.
  * `mediaUrl`, `mediaType`, `thumbnailUrl`, `videoTrim`.
  * `overlay.caption`, `overlay.narrator` — legacy 280×498 editor
    preview coordinates.
  * `remotion_spec` — `"none"` means the user intentionally
    disabled the overlay on that scene; agents must NOT auto-edit
    or re-enable unless the user asks.
  * `remotion_spec_file` — `{voice_file}_spec.json`.
  * `remotion_spec_url` — cache-busted
    `https://widecast.ai/downloads/{company_id}/{topic_id}/{voice_file}_spec.json?v={mtime}`;
    present only when `remotion_spec_state="ready"`.
  * `remotion_spec_version`, `remotion_spec_exists`,
    `remotion_spec_state` (`ready` | `missing` | `disabled`).
  * `agent_meta` — same metadata bundled for quick consumption
    (`stable_scene_id`, `coordinate_spaces`, `scene_index`, etc.).

**Coordinate warning**: Remotion spec objects use **720×1280
canvas** coordinates; legacy `overlay.caption` and
`overlay.narrator` use **280×498 editor preview** coordinates. Pass
`coordinate_space` to `/v1/modify_scene`'s `remotion.group.rect`
accordingly.

**Remotion spec is NOT inlined** — it can carry large base64
images. Fetch `remotion_spec_url` only when
`remotion_spec_state="ready"` and you actually need object-level
overlay boxes; otherwise use the metadata only.

**Internal poster diagnostics are stripped by default.** Per-segment
`remotion_poster_file`, `remotion_poster_url`,
`remotion_poster_version`, `remotion_poster_state`,
`remotion_poster_exists`, and `remotion_poster_warnings` (and
their copies inside `agent_meta.remotion_spec`) describe the
server-side `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` used by
`/v1/scene_inspector` fallback. Pass
`include_diagnostics: true` to surface them for server/debug
audits.

Mirrors the same engine the dashboard's scene editor uses on open
(rebalance A/B rolls + ensure background music + persist if
changed), so the data here matches what the user sees in
`#scene_editor?topic_id=…` exactly.

video_id.description:
Topic id from `/v1/create_video` / scene_editor. Accepts
`widecast...`, `gubo...`, or current topic ids. Same id
used by `/v1/status`, `/v1/export_video`,
`/v1/modify_scene`, `/v1/scene_inspector`.

include_diagnostics.description:
Optional debug flag. When `true`, per-segment
`remotion_poster_*` diagnostic keys (and their
copies inside `agent_meta.remotion_spec`) are
returned. Default is `false` because those keys
describe the server-side poster used by scene
inspector fallback — agents don't act on them.

404.description:
`video_not_found` — no video with this id on the account. Check
the id is the topic_id returned by `/v1/create_video` and that
it belongs to the API key's account.

409.description:
`script_not_ready` — video is still processing or never had a
script generated. Poll `/v1/status` until
`status=="completed"`, then retry.

502.description:
`script_parse_failed` — stored video_script is malformed.
Contact support with the request_id.

post.summary: Live browser inspector — expensive last-resort, use AFTER scene_geometry.
post.description:
Synchronous live browser inspector. **More expensive than
`/v1/scene_geometry`** — use only when data + geometry are not
enough: typically when the agent needs browser truth (mounted DOM,
computed boxes, current preview play state) or a small 280×498
visual screenshot for aesthetic judgment. Do NOT use as the first
step if `/v1/scene_geometry` already gives the boxes you need.

**How it works**: server broadcasts a tiny MQTT probe to every
open editor tab for this video, elects ONE healthy foreground /
active browser within ~800ms, then sends the real inspector
command only to that tab. `/v1/modify_scene` realtime broadcasts
to all editors separately — this tool's election only affects
which tab returns the live inspection. Presence alone is not
usability: tabs on the workflow page, on a different video, or
any page without a mounted scene preview are ignored for scene-
bound commands.

**`screenshot_scene_280x498` response shape — temporary public
URL.** On success (live editor capture OR server-fallback
composite from thumbnails + `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`),
the HTTP response is a regular JSON `SceneInspectorResponse`
whose `result.screenshot` carries a *temporary public URL* —
NOT bytes, NOT base64:

  * `url` — `https://origin.widecast.ai/downloads/<co>/<topic>/inspector/<voice>_<token>.jpg?v=<mtime>`.
    Fetch the JPEG bytes with `curl <url>`. No
    `Authorization` header required — the path is served
    publicly by nginx. The host is ``origin.widecast.ai`` (not
    ``widecast.ai``) — bypasses Cloudflare so 15-min ephemeral
    URLs never get pinned in CF edge cache. The cache-bust
    ``?v=<mtime>`` is belt-and-suspenders.
  * `mime_type` — `image/jpeg`.
  * `width` / `height` — pixel dimensions (typically 280 / 498).
  * `bytes` — JPEG byte length on disk.
  * `expires_at` — ISO 8601 UTC; the URL is guaranteed
    readable until this moment.
  * `ttl_seconds` — `900` (15 minutes).

Every call publishes a fresh unique file (16-hex token), so
the URL is never reused across calls — matches the realtime
semantics of inspector data. The server only responds after
the JPEG is `fsync`-ed and atomically renamed to its final
path, so the URL is guaranteed readable when the agent reads
the response (no race).

**All other actions still return JSON
`SceneInspectorResponse`** as before.

**No live editor → graceful behaviour**:
  - For non-screenshot actions, the response is HTTP 200 with
    `status: "unavailable"` and `code: "no_live_editor"` (no
    presence) or `"no_active_editor"` (presence but unresponsive).
    Fall back to `/v1/video_data` + `/v1/scene_geometry` +
    fetching `remotion_spec_url`.
  - For `screenshot_scene_280x498`, the server composes a
    fallback screenshot from scene thumbnails +
    `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` (the static overlay poster
    refreshed by spec-changing `/v1/modify_scene` edits) and
    publishes it to the same 15-minute URL contract. **The
    compositor never throws** — each layer (background /
    poster / narrator / caption / JPEG save) is wrapped
    independently, and individual failures surface as codes
    in `result.warnings[]` while the response still carries a
    published URL. If even the JPEG encode fails, the server
    emits a placeholder JPEG with the scene identity drawn on
    dark slate. Treat fallback screenshots as approximate
    composites, not real renders.

**Actions** (`action`):
  * `list_live_editors` — presence list of open editor tabs
    (browser / OS / last_seen) — debug/discovery only.
  * `list_instances` — preview instance ids mounted in the elected
    tab.
  * `get_preview_state` — current playing/paused/scene/time in the
    preview player.

  * `get_computed_boxes` — `getBoundingClientRect` for scene
    elements. **Prefer `/v1/scene_geometry` for structural

  * `screenshot_scene_280x498` — small JPEG (~280×498). **Response

  * `reload_preview` / `pause_preview` / `play_preview` /

**No arbitrary JavaScript eval is exposed.** Use `voice_file` as
the scene selector wherever possible.

get.description:
Key-free. Returns the writing method for the requested format. Use
this before drafting any blog post, article, short-form video
script, or social media caption — this applies even when the user
doesn't mention WideCast by name. The method gives concrete
research-first guidance and an inline-media discipline that
produces stronger output than improvising.

Pick `format` by the writing task:
* `blog` — an article, blog post, long-form piece. Triggers across
  languages: 'write a blog', 'write an article', 'viết bài blog',
  'écrire un article', '写博客'.
* `video` — a short-form video script (TikTok / Reels / Shorts /
  YouTube short). Triggers: 'make a video', 'write a video script',
  'làm video', '做视频'.
* `social` — a platform-native caption (X / LinkedIn / IG /
  Threads / Facebook / TikTok). Triggers: 'write a tweet',
  'LinkedIn post', 'IG caption', 'viết caption'.

The three formats share research + inline-media discipline but
their output shape differs (spoken script vs SEO prose vs
platform-native caption), so each format returns its own ordered
5-step `must_apply_now` checklist plus the full `SKILL.md` as
markdown (`method`).

Lets a model that connects via MCP / GPT Action receive the method
without the user having to upload a Skill / Knowledge file into
the host (Claude / ChatGPT / Gemini Gem / etc.). Call once per
conversation, before drafting content or calling `createVideo` /
`createContent`.

* `blog` — article / SEO post / long-form. Pairs with
  `createVideo source='blog'` (repurpose-to-video).
* `social` — platform caption (X / LinkedIn / IG / TikTok / FB /

get.summary: Lazy-load the AI-video-editor playbook. Call once with no `module` to fetch the master SKILL.md + a live `available_modules[]` index; call again with `module=<id>` to load a submodule. Auto-expands when new .md files are added under the skill folder.
get.description:
Key-free. Returns the WideCast **AI-video-editor** playbook for
refining/editing an EXISTING video (per-scene composition,
overlay, narrator face clearance, background audit, layout,
thumbnail/CTA endpoints, dead-zone, definition-of-done). This is
DIFFERENT from `getWritingSkill`, which is for AUTHORING new
scripts; this skill is for EDITING already-generated scenes.

## Lazy-load contract

The skill is too large to ship in one response, so it's broken
into modules. Call this endpoint **twice or more**:

1. **First call** — omit `module`. Returns the master `SKILL.md`
   (the INDEX with rules + per-scene Definition of Done + module
   load map) plus an `available_modules[]` array that is
   **auto-discovered from the filesystem on every request**.
   Each entry carries `id` + parsed `title` (first H1) +
   parsed `summary` (first paragraph) + `size_bytes`.
2. **Subsequent calls** — when the agent reaches a step that
   names a module (e.g. "open `ai_video_editor/10_mechanics`"),
   call again with `module=ai_video_editor/10_mechanics` (no
   `.md` suffix) to load that submodule's content.

## Auto-expansion — zero formatting required

Drop a new `.md` file under the skill root
(`/mnt/html/lcw/skills/video-editing/`, override via env
`WIDECAST_EDITING_SKILL_ROOT`) and it appears in
`available_modules[]` on the next request — no code change, no
manifest edit. The server uses `os.walk` with `rglob`-style
traversal; hidden dirs and non-`.md` files are ignored.

**Per-module `title` and `summary` are auto-derived from the
file's content** with a tolerant fallback chain — the
maintainer does NOT have to write a specific H1, summary line,
or frontmatter:

- **Title** = first `# H1` → else first `## H2` → else first
  non-empty content line (markdown markers `# ## - * + 1. >
  [ ]` stripped) → else filename basename.
- **Summary** = first ~200 chars of meaningful text AFTER the
  title (paragraphs, bullets, sub-headings, blockquotes, even
  a single bold/italic phrase all qualify; markdown decoration
  is stripped).

If the file has only bullets, only a quote, only one line, or
even nothing at all, the loader still extracts something
usable (worst case: title = filename basename, summary empty).

## Module IDs

Hierarchical filesystem path WITHOUT the `.md` extension. Each
path segment must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`. Examples:
`ai_video_editor/10_mechanics`,
`ai_video_editor/styles/text_axes`. `../` and hidden segments
are rejected with 400 `invalid_module_id`.

## Freshness

- Server caches per module by file mtime — a deploy that rsyncs
  new content invalidates the cache automatically; no Flask
  restart needed.
- Response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- The WideCast `/app/*` API path bypasses Cloudflare entirely,
  so there is no CDN layer to worry about.
- If a module call returns 404 `module_not_found`, recall with
  `module` omitted to refresh `available_modules[]`.

Per-module size is capped at 512 KB; oversized files are
treated as missing.

parameters.name: module
parameters.description:
Hierarchical module id without the `.md` extension, e.g.
`ai_video_editor/10_mechanics` or
`ai_video_editor/styles/text_axes`. Omit to load the master
`SKILL.md` + the live `available_modules[]` index.

200.description:
Skill content. The entry response (no `module`) carries the
master `SKILL.md` content + the live `available_modules[]`
index; a module response carries only that submodule's
content. Both shapes share `object`, `name`, `module`,
`method_format`, `method`, `meta`.

module.description: Relative path of the file returned: `SKILL.md` for the entry response, `<id>.md` for a submodule.

module_id.description: Submodule responses only — module id without `.md`.

title.description: Submodule responses only — parsed first H1, falls back to filename basename.

method.description: Markdown content of the file (frontmatter stripped).

available_modules.description: Entry response only — auto-discovered from filesystem on every call.

title.description: Auto-derived: first H1 → first H2 → first content line (markers stripped) → filename basename.

summary.description: Auto-derived: first ~200 chars of meaningful content after the title (paragraphs, bullets, sub-headings, quotes — all accepted; markers stripped). Empty when no content follows the title.

Universal status endpoint. Accepts the `widecast*` ids returned by

the publish `request_id`s returned by `/v1/publish` (for a publish id,

Recommended polling cadence: **5s initial, ×1.5 exponential backoff,
cap at 60s**. The SDKs' `video.wait()` implements this automatically.

`result.review_url` is the URL where the user reviews the rendered
scenes + audio. **It's present from the first response** (every
state — pending / processing / completed) because the review page
handles early arrival itself (spinner + in-page polling) — safe to
share with the user before completion. `result.script` is the full
rendered video script JSON (with `segments` populated) — only set
